messages:
Alex Chen: Heads-up — kicking off the private deployment roadmap thread (VPC control plane, on‑prem packaging, air‑gapped constraints). Need to align on Q2 OKRs, launch criteria, and what we call the MVP vs. stretch. Customers pushing: HealthCorp and FinServInc for on‑prem/air‑gapped.

Priya Patel: Quick proposal: MVP = VPC control plane (customer VPC peering / private CP endpoints) + an opinionated on‑prem package (Helm chart + offline tarball for kube nodes). Air‑gapped support (no external outbound) is stretch for the MVP and gated by security signoff. Thoughts?

Samir Rao: From eng-infra perspective: VPC CP MVP feasible if we scope to AWS first (cross‑account role + PrivateLink). Need KMS integration for secrets and audit logs from day 1. On‑prem packaging: Helm + CRDs + a small operator seems fine. Air‑gap adds a lot — image registry mirror workflow, offline dependency management, signed bundles. Estimate: MVP 8 weeks, air‑gapped +4–6 weeks.

Maya Gomez: Sales: health/finsvc customers are pushing air‑gapped as MUST for procurement. We have two pilots that will sign MSA if air‑gap is supported in 3 months. Is there a compromise?

Priya Patel: Negotiation idea: ship MVP with an "offline install path" that supports mirror tarballs but with limited automation. That would let sales promise an air‑gap path while we iterate on a fully automated mirrored registry and signed bundles. Acceptance criteria for "offline install path" should be explicit.

Liam O'Neill: Security: offline install path is acceptable if we provide a signed artifact bundle, checksum verification, and an offline verification script that uses customer KMS/HSM. Full air‑gapped mode needs enforceable policy for no external calls (no telemetry), and a hardened node image. We should add formal threat model and pen test step to the launch criteria.

Olivia Park: Product ops / runbooks: we need runbook templates (deploy, rollback, data migration) and a customer test lab where we can validate an on‑prem install end‑to‑end before shipping. Also require documentation for lifecycle: upgrades, cert rotation, backups.

Samir Rao: Tech dependencies list (short):
```
- AWS PrivateLink & cross-account IAM roles
- KMS / HSM integration (AWS KMS + HSM compatibility for on‑prem)
- Image mirroring tool (skopeo / registry mirror) for offline path
- Signed bundle format (TUF or cosign) for integrity
- Operator + Helm + CRDs for orchestration
```

Priya Patel: OKRs suggestion for Q2:
- Objective: Launch private deployment MVP for early enterprise customers
- KR1: 2 pilot customers onboarded to VPC control plane by end of Q2
- KR2: On‑prem packaged installer validated in our test lab with documented runbook
- KR3: <25% manual steps for offline install (measured by runbook steps)
Would like input on feasibility from eng.

Samir Rao: Feasible but aggressive. If we cut scope (no automated registry mirroring) we can hit Q2 pilots. With full air‑gapped automation we slip to late Q2/early Q3.

Maya Gomez: Sales asks for clear launch criteria to communicate to customers. Can we codify a checklist for "pilot ready" vs "GA"?

Alex Chen: Proposed launch criteria — Pilot Ready: 1) Deployable into customer VPC with private control plane endpoints; 2) On‑prem installer works in our test lab; 3) KMS integration and basic audit logs; 4) Runbook + support rotation. GA: 1) 2 successful pilot completions; 2) Automated offline bundle tooling + signed images; 3) Security pen test completed; 4) SLA + docs.

Liam O'Neill: Add to GA: telemetry opt‑out verified, no hardcoded outbound URLs. Compliance checklist for FinServInc (PCI/GLBA) will require additional controls — note as dependent work.

Olivia Park: Who owns the test lab setup and the first pilot?

Priya Patel: Eng‑platform will own CP + packaging. Samir + team will provision test lab with a mirror of customer VPC. Olivia / Solutions will run pilot onboarding playbook with Sales.

Samir Rao: I'll own test lab + deployment validation. Estimate lab ready in 2 weeks if no blockers. Need access to a customer‑like network diagram from Sales.

Maya Gomez: Sending FinServInc network diagram now (DM). HealthCorp still needs legal ok — pushing that.

Alex Chen: Risks / blockers captured: 1) KMS/HSM integration complexity; 2) Image signing & mirror workflow; 3) Security signoff timeline for air‑gapped; 4) Support/training for on‑prem ops. Mitigations: phased approach, explicit customer letters for pilots, and temporary professional services add‑on.

Priya Patel: Requesting decisions needed by end of week: A) MVP scope (include offline install path yes/no); B) Pilot compress timeline commitment; C) Resource commit (engineer FTEs for 8 weeks).

Samir Rao: We can commit to A=YES (offline install path), B=pilot timeline best effort (need sales to lock pilot windows), C=allocate 2 FTEs from eng‑platform + 1 infra for networking for 8 weeks.

Olivia Park: Ops can provide runbook templates and 1 solutions engineer for pilots.

Alex Chen: OK — I'll document the roadmap slice and push to the product roadmap board. Action items: Samir to spin up test lab (due +2w), Priya to write acceptance criteria doc (due +5d), Olivia to draft pilot playbook (due +7d), Maya to secure customer timelines.

deploy-bot: Deployment checklist created: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/private-deploy-checklist (auto note).

Priya Patel: Thanks — will follow up with a short RFC with scope + acceptance criteria tomorrow. If anyone has objections to MVP scope, reply here before EOD Friday. :thumbsup:

Alex Chen: Thanks everyone — feel free to DM for clarifications.
